text: I stood on the north quay Wednesday morning as crews at the Tessaly Fjord tidal plant confirmed the facility is rated at 95 megawatts, according to the placard bolted beside the control room door. Operations manager Lina Voss told me the figure matches the plant’s final commissioning documents and that all four turbine housings are now online. She said the first full-capacity test was logged before dawn, with output steady through the 6:40 a.m. tide surge. I watched technicians check the intake screens while a supervisor noted the reading on a handheld meter. The plant, opened last autumn, now supplies power to the Baywater grid from the fjord channel.
